text.p: Lithuanian newspapers carried the following reports in their Monday editions. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy:

- An explosion early Saturday morning rocked a resort home belonging to the interior ministry at the seaside resort town of Palanga. No one was hurt in the blast, which caused 15,000 litas worth of damage. Police suspect the bomb was a warning of some kind and not meant to inflict injury.
- The Patriarch of the Russian Orthodox Church, Alexei II, gave mass at the Church of the Holy Spirit in Vilnius.
- Finance Minister Algirdas Shemeta spent almost five million litas to renovate his office.
- The price for Lithuanian Gas' 66 million litas share issue will be no less than 1.65 litas per share.
- Timber production decreased by nine percent in Lithuania in the first six months of the year compared to the same period last year.
- The institute for social research said the poverty line was 250 litas a month.
- The state tax inspectorate wants to ban the sale of tobacco products from kiosks because it is too easy to hide income generated from tobacco sales.
- By October 1, there will be a 15,000 tonne sugar surplus left from last year's production.

- Vilniuas Bank says it is active in the securities market but has not invested in any companies apart from its daughter firm VB Leasing. The bank plans to set up special funds for investment projects in the future.
- The first stage of the reconstruction of Siauliai airport has been completed and the facility is classified to handle all aircraft. The airport still needs $260 million to finish reconstruction.
- Real wages increased by 2.8 percent in June and the average salary rose by 3.4 percent.
- Privatisation auctions for state-owned stakes in 29 enterprises will start on August 18 at the national stock exchange and be held every Monday until September 29.
